column1: # Generated by check_dead_exports.sh, which also gates it.  Every row is
# an exported symbol that no OTHER production translation unit
# references.  References from anything under tests/ do not count: a
# test calling a function directly is exactly what hid this class of
# defect, so counting tests would defeat the gate.
# THIS LIST IS EXPECTED TO SHRINK AND MUST NEVER GROW.  Wiring a dead
# procedure into the daemon makes its row fail as "allowlisted symbol is
# now referenced"; that failure is the intended signal, not an obstacle.
# Resolve it by deleting the row, or regenerate the whole file:
# Regeneration preserves the category and note of every symbol already
# listed, so review work is never lost.
# class -- how the census sees the symbol
#   unreferenced  no production unit names it: dead code.
#   file-local    named only inside its own defining unit; it is
# category -- whether the row is a PROBLEM, and if so which kind.
# The distinction that matters is between a procedure that OUGHT to run
# and cannot, and surface that is dead because nothing in this product
# is supposed to call it.  The first four categories are problems.
#   dead-mandatory       A PROBLEM, and the worst kind.  An implemented,
#                        -- or this daemon own documentation -- says
#                        with no production caller: it executes in no
#                        shipped code path however green its tests are.
#                        Fix it by wiring it to a real caller -- never by
#                        inventing a caller no code path reaches, which
#                        converts a dead export into a lie and silences
#                        the only instrument that can see it.
#   operator-surface-gap A PROBLEM, but not one a wiring change can fix.
#                        The procedure is implemented and correct and
#                        there is no code path to it because no operator
#                        verb, config key or protocol field can ask for
#                        it.  The note must size the missing surface.
#                        Often paired with a parser for a response we can
#                        never provoke -- look for that when triaging.
#   superseded           A PROBLEM only in that it still exists.  A
#                        duplicate of a newer entry point that the daemon
#                        uses instead.  Delete it; the note names the
#                        replacement.  Several are also strictly weaker
#                        than what replaced them (missing locking or
#                        missing guards), so keeping them is a trap.
#   unreviewed           PRESUMED A PROBLEM.  Seeded by the census and
#                        not yet triaged.  Reclassify, with a note, as
#   over-exported        Not a problem, just wrong linkage.  The symbol
#                        HAS callers, all inside its own translation
#                        unit, so it should be static.  Derived from the
#                        file-local class, not from judgement.  Note that
#                        the unreferenced class OVER-REPORTS the reverse
#                        way: these daemons link as PIE, the assembler
#                        resolves an intra-unit call to a global function
#                        without emitting a relocation, and the readelf
#                        pass cannot see it.  So an unreferenced row may
#                        still have same-unit callers; check by grep
#   client-role-api      Not a problem.  Client-model entry point for a
#                        role this product does not implement; meshd
#                        only serves these models.  Kept as API.
#   public-library-api   Not a problem.  Exported through the installed
#                        ble.h and libble.3; consumers are out of tree.
#   simulator-api        Not a problem.  mesh_sim harness surface,
#                        driven by tests and tools, not by meshd.
#   dead-by-design       Not a problem, but it must be argued per symbol
#                        in the note: "it is an API" is not a reason.
#                        Unreachable because of what this product IS --
#                        a transport it does not carry, a spec procedure
#                        that does not exist, a controller test-mode
#                        command, an accessor whose contract is unsafe
#   deliberately-dead    Not a problem: REMOVED ON PURPOSE, and wiring it
#                        back would reintroduce a defect.  The note must
#                        say which defect.  Annotate or delete; never
# 541 rows: dead-mandatory 185, operator-surface-gap 30, superseded 13, over-exported 63, client-role-api 134, public-library-api 83, simulator-api 24, dead-by-design 8, deliberately-dead 1
